summary: The note argues that Southeast Asian cuisine is evolving through fusion, technology, sustainability and education, illustrated by dated 2023 examples from chefs and institutions across the region and beyond. Innovators such as Linh Tran, Aarav Mehta, Marco Santoso and Aishah Bidin reinterpret classic dishes with modern techniques while claiming to honor tradition. It concludes that food is a cultural conversation and that tradition and innovation can coexist.
one_line: Chefs, apps and schools in 2023 are reshaping traditional Southeast Asian dishes through fusion, technology and sustainability while respecting heritage.
key_facts: Chef Linh Tran, owner of the Hanoi restaurant "Đổi Mới" (meaning "innovation" in Vietnamese), spoke at the "Flavors of the Future" conference in Singapore on September 10th, 2023.
Linh Tran uses sous-vide to cook the beef for her pho, so each slice is precisely cooked, departing from the traditional method of simmering beef in large pots for hours.
Linh Tran says, "Innovation does not mean disrespect; it is a homage that respects the past and embraces the future."

On September 26th, 2023, Chef Aarav Mehta of the Bangkok eatery "Nuad Thai" was described as using molecular gastronomy to turn turmeric, lemongrass and galangal into edible balloons that burst in diners' mouths.
Aarav Mehta serves a deconstructed 'Green Curry Chicken' on a slate of locally sourced limestones, a nod to the Thai landscape.
On October 12th, 2023, Indonesian food blogger Jessica Kezia chronicled her visit to "The Archipelago," a newly opened fusion restaurant in Sydney.
Chef Marco Santoso, a native Indonesian who loves Italian cooking, created a 'Rendang Lasagna' at The Archipelago, with house-made pasta layers and creamy béchamel replacing coconut milk.

On November 1st, 2023, the tech start-up "GastroTech" made headlines in Jakarta with an AI app that suggests contemporary variations of traditional Indonesian recipes and adapts them to modern diets such as veganism or keto.
The GastroTech app can personalize gado-gado with quinoa and kale.
On December 5th, 2023, Malaysian chef Aishah Bidin of "Kebun Bistro" in Kuala Lumpur presented a farm-to-table concept, serving 'Nasi Ulam' with herbs and vegetables from her rooftop garden.
Aishah Bidin introduces lab-grown meat into her dishes to reduce the carbon footprint.
On December 20th, 2023, students of "The Saigon Culinary Institute" showcased year-end projects in which they were encouraged to reconstruct traditional dishes rather than just replicate them.
Top graduate Ivy Nguyen said, "To preserve our culinary traditions, we have to understand both their roots and their potential paths."
